name: QQ Show (QQ秀)
blurb: Tencent's paid avatar dress-up for QQ users, launched in 2003 and bought with Q coins
title: What Is QQ Show (QQ秀)? Tencent's 2003 Avatar Dress-Up
description: QQ Show (QQ秀) was Tencent's avatar dress-up service from 2003: clothes and backgrounds bought with Q coins. Folded away in 2021, it returned with AI in 2026.
answer: QQ Show (QQ秀, QQ Xiu) is a virtual avatar service inside Tencent's QQ messenger: you dress a cartoon figure in hairstyles, clothes, accessories and backgrounds bought with Q coins, and friends see it in the chat window. It launched on 24 January 2003, started charging two months later and became one of Tencent's main early money-makers. The PC version was folded away in 2021, and in January 2026 Tencent announced its return in an AI-powered form.

body: QQ was China's dominant instant messenger in the 2000s, and every account came with a basic cartoon figure. In the QQ Show mall you bought items one by one: hats, hairstyles, tops, trousers, shoes, things to hold, and a background scene, or a complete outfit. Most items cost Q coins, Tencent's virtual currency, and some expired after a set time.
Your outfit stood at the side of the chat window, so every friend you talked to saw it. Changing clothes was a way of being seen, much like a profile picture or a game skin today.
Red Diamond (红钻), a membership launched in 2004 for 10 yuan a month, unlocked a range of exclusive clothes and lit up a red diamond badge on your profile.

head: Year
What happened
rows: Trial launch on 24 January, paid from about two months later; reportedly about 5 million buyers in the first half year
A survey cited by Jiemian found over 40% of 355 million registered users had bought QQ Show items
Mobile QQ adds a similar animated avatar feature
QQ Show disappears from PC QQ 9.5.2; Tencent says it is only folded inside the chat window
On 24 January Tencent announces QQ Show's return, with avatars generated by AI from uploaded photos

sections.h: Where it came from and what happened
body: Tech media in China report that the idea was modeled on the avatar shop of the South Korean site Sayclub, and that a Korean company helped draw the first characters.

QQ Show belonged to the desktop era. On phones the chat screen had no room for a standing figure, so it slid to the margins: Red Diamond closed, the PC version was hidden, and Tencent kept trying new forms, from animated mobile avatars to a 3D version to the 2026 AI relaunch. The classic flat dress-up and the clothes people bought for it now survive mostly in old screenshots.

Judging a friend's spending by their clothes and background

faq.a: Tencent announced its return in January 2026 in a new AI-based form that generates avatars from photos. The old flat dress-up version is no longer the main form.
Q coins were Tencent's virtual currency, bought with real money and spent on QQ Show items and other paid QQ services.
A QQ Show membership launched in 2004 for 10 yuan a month that gave access to exclusive clothes. Renewals stopped in 2020.
